The City will be conducting public meeting in – person in the Council Chambers.  To participate in the City of
Commerce ‘public meetings and provide public comments, please follow these steps:

1. Participate in person during the meeting, and submit public comments card if you would like to speak on any
item on the agenda or any other topic.

Watch or Listen: Meetings are broadcast/streamed live on the City of  Commerce’s Facebook:
https://www.facebook.com/City-of-Commerce-123903054365151/?ref . Archived, on-demand  video of each meeting
is maintained on the City’s Facebook as part of the public record.

2. Submit Comments before the Meeting: Members of the public can provide public comment by sending an
e-mail to cityclerk@ci.commerce.ca.us for City Council meetings. Written public comments will be acknowledged
and summarized during the public comment period by the City Clerk or the Mayor.

PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called meeting to order at 5:06 p.m.

ROLL CALL Councilmember Rebollo arrived at 5:08 p.m.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda.  

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:08 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:05 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT The City Attorney Tapia provided a report on the outcome of the closed session.

Item #1A and B was discussed, and staff provided a presentation. The City Council provided direction on this item, but no reportable action was taken.

Item #2.D. was not discussed during the closed session.

Items #2.A., 2.B and 2.C, #3 and #4 were also discussed during the closed session. Staff made a presentation on these items, and the City Council provided feedback. However, no reportable action was taken on these items.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called regular meeting to order at 6:07 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE City Manager Cisneros led the Pledge of Allegiance. 

INVOCATION Councilmember Garcia offered the invocation. 

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Recognition of the Commerce Dance Teams for their Achievements during 2023, and Winning Dance National Championship in Las Vegas, Nevada Mayor Argumedo and Councilmembers recognized Dance Teams for their achievements ad winning dance National Championship in Las Vegas, Nevada. 

PUBLIC COMMENT Brian Davis, a Real Estate Attorney, has stated that he is currently representing the interests of certain local businesses in matters related to commercial leases. Specifically, Mr. Davis referred to Fenix Enterprises, which has leased commercial space from the City, and Martin Fierro. He alleged that Mr. Fierro has received preferential treatment and has been able to lease land below market value. Mr. Davis further added that there was an article published in the San Diego Tribune on this issue, and they will continue to investigate the matter.

In another matter, Gloria Nezahualgoyotl submitted a request seeking information on why the Transportation Director was authorized to use a vehicle and which meetings he attended during the Covid pandemic, specifically regional meetings. She questioned why the Transportation Director was given a vehicle while other executives were not. All directors should be treated equally, and Ms. Nezahualgoyotl sought clarification on this matter.




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Councilmember Rebollo pulled item #4. and Councilmember Garcia pulled item #6 for discussion. 

item 34- Councilmember Rebollo requested that items related to disability causes and similar proclamations be placed under presentations. After reading the proclamation, Mayor Argumedo moved to approve it, which was seconded by Councilmember Lainez. The motion was passed with a vote of 5-0, with Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamirano, and Mayor Argumedo voting in favor.

Regarding Item #6, Councilmember Garcia raised a concern about how the project would impact the City of Commerce. In response, City Manager Cisneros stated that the analysis of the project is ongoing, and they will provide more information to the City Council later.  Vice Mayor Altamirano moved, seconded by Councilmember Garcia, to adopt a Resolution approving an Agreement with California High Speed Authority and Amendments to Consultant Agreements with Southstar Engineering & Consulting, Inc., JM Diaz, Inc. and Mott Macdonald, LLC for a High Speed Rail Project.   The motion was passed with a vote of 5-0, with Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamirano, and Mayor Argumedo voting in favor.






3.. Approval of Minutes

6.. Agreement with the California High Speed Rail Authority and Amendments to On-Call Consultants Associated with the Project

5.. FY 2021-22 Pavement Rehabilitation Project Acceptance

4.. A Proclamation Declaring the Month of April 2023 as Limb Loss Awareness Month

2.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 17A, 17B, and 17C

SCHEDULED MATTERS

9.. Award of Construction Contract to California Commercial Pools, Inc. for the Brenda Villa Aquatic Center Pool Filtration System Replacement Project  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano The Acting Director of Public Works Nila gave an overview of the staff report. The report stated that the filtration units were leaking from the bottom and the UV system needed to be replaced since they were over 20 years old. Due to the higher cost of replacement, the department was requesting an additional appropriation to award the contract for this work.


10.. Organizational Assignments for Councilmembers The City Council reviewed organizational assignments and requested the City Clerk to confirm the attendance of the appointee for the Vector Control organization. 

Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk Shumway stated that the Mayor becomes automatically the representative of the County Sanitation District, and Mayor Argumedo is the Board Member.

The Council made the following changes to the organizational assignments:

Southern California Association of Government (SCAG): Councilmember Lainez was appointed, with Councilmember Rebollo as the alternate.
Employment Task Force: Mayor Argumedo was appointed

Rest of assignments stayed the same as the year before.  


8.. Modifications to the Existing First-Time Homebuyer 2.0 Program Guidelines item #8 was continued to the next meeting.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Rebollo requested an adjournment for the next meeting for a resident (name would be sent later) and thanked sports teams for their championships and being so competitive, and representing the City. Mayor Rebollo announced that the hiring of recreation leaders almost finished, which would allow most recreation program being brought back, and thanked residents for their patience. 

Councilmember Garcia attended the Joe Lozano dedication event at Bristow Park and praised staff's work on Mixmaster that really helped with the traffic control.  

Councilmember Lainez agreed that work performed at Mixmaster regarding striping was great, and stated that he also attended Joe Lozano dedication event.  Additionally, he attended a fundraiser for the Commerce Aces at Rosewood Park, which was organized by Ester Zavala, and commended her for a job well done. Councilmember Lainez also participated in a library volunteer recognition breakfast. Finally, he requested that staff provide an update on the hiring efforts for Parks and Recreation at the next meeting.

Vice Mayor Altamirano attended the Joe Lozano event and a Mass Timber conference in Colorado.  Vice Mayor Altamirano requested a presentation on the subject for the City Council. He also suggested creating a separate Arts in Public Places subcommittee and recommended bringing back the Wayfinding project.

Mayor Argumedo attended the Joe Lozano's ceremony, a library volunteer breakfast, and asked for clarification to be provided regarding who was invited to that event.  Mayor Argumedo reported that he went to City of Aguascalientes (Sister City), and it was a great visit.
   
The City Council reconvened to Closed session at 7:06pm 

ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 9:42 p.m.

Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.

7.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Duarte presented a comparison of crime statistics between the City of Cudahy, the City of Maywood, and the East Los Angeles area.
